problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=(1-x)(y+2)^{2}.$ What are the missing entries in the following sign table of $f(x,y)?$

| $y>-2$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-2$ |  |  |
|  | $x<1$ | $x>1$ |
worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=1$ and $y=-2.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/345665733b6554a7cea9b54a4ca4e93b6d478d67231cfaf3f6180cf0a75c4b1a.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/4058b0f027297faf71756da7cad372b76aae980657f053b95318115889c1d614.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $1-x$ | $(y+2)^{2}$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(0,-1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(2,-1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(0,-3)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(2,-3)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |

 

Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/fc54a4044465d485d4eb55aa8dd81c0e952e8dd56528bc2874bcc67dcffbf3c8.png)

Finally, we fill in the required sign table.

| $y>-2$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-2$ | $+$ | $-$ |
|  | $x<1$ | $x>1$ |
